notes: A one-cutscene Abyssea storyline flag. The single sub-bullet says the quest 'cannot be completed it can only be flagged', which is a property of the quest and not a step -- it also means no hand-in exists and none is invented. The Abyssite of the cosmos resolves as key item 1443 and would be tempting as evidence, but it is the header's Reward, so by rule it proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done; with a single step there is nothing for it to advance to anyway, so evidence stays null. Fame 'Abyssea' is not one of the nine fame regions, so region is null and only raw is kept. 'Abyssea - Empyreal Paradox' is the full zone name and resolves as zone 255 -- the bare 'Empyreal Paradox' is a DIFFERENT zone (36), so the wiki's long form is the one recorded.

notes: Two bullets, two steps, both on the same Moblin -- one marker, with readiness looking ahead across them. The description sends you to Davoi to search for Zeelozok and names the Orcish overlord, and a verb-scanner would happily manufacture a travel step to Davoi and a talk step on Zeelozok; the WALKTHROUGH does neither. notes: Three bullets, two steps. Bullet 1 ('Obtain a Mythril Sallet from the auction house or for 437 Sparks') is a shopping instruction for the header's Item Reqs, not a rung: making it step 1 with the sallet as evidence would leave the quest with NO marker at all until the player happened to buy one, because an auction house purchase has no targetable entity. Folding it into the trade step loses nothing -- `items` on a trade already tells the runtime that holding the sallet means ready to hand in -- and both bullet numbers are kept on that step so the merge stays auditable. The two steps are consecutive on Detzo, so they are one marker either way. The sub-bullet about the sallet being handed back is an outcome and an inventory warning, not a step.

steps.note: the sallet comes from the auction house (Armor > Head) or 437 Sparks -- bullet 1 merged in here. He gives it back afterwards, so keep an inventory slot free.

notes: The header names Galmut as the giver, but the walkthrough is explicit that you reach him 'by interacting with the Door: House targetable location' -- Galmut is behind that door, and the door is the entity you actually click. Both names resolve, so this is a marker MOVE and not a loss: start is set to Door: House at the same zone and grid, with the header string kept verbatim in start.raw. Bullet 2 ('This quest will then be completed') is an outcome, not a rung. The 'Optional:' line is unnumbered on the page -- it follows bullet 2 -- and is recorded as source bullet 3 so the count stays honest; it names Collet but gives no zone, and Collet resolves as an unambiguous key, so the step keeps a marker with a null zone rather than having one guessed for it. VERIFY: demoted to medium -- the ladder is readable but the page is both self-disagreeing and incomplete, and two calls here want a human eye. First, the giver has been MOVED off the header's Galmut onto Door: House. The walkthrough does support it and both names resolve, but the only evidence that Galmut is not himself standing at (G-7) is the single word 'by' in one sentence; if he is a standing NPC the marker now points at the wrong entity, so this is a marker move made on thin wording rather than a clear-cut case like a cutscene-only summon. Second, the page never says where Collet is -- her zone and grid are null because the source omits them, not because they were dropped here, so that optional rung cannot be placed at all. The 'Optional:' line is also unnumbered on the page and its source_bullets value of 3 is a synthetic index, not the page's own.

steps.note: clicking the door is how you speak to Galmut; the previous quest must be complete first. Bullet 2 only says the quest then completes, which is an outcome.

the page's own 'Optional:' line, which is unnumbered and counted here as the third top-level line. A short cutscene after the quest is already complete; the page gives no zone or grid for Collet, so neither is invented.

notes: The whole walkthrough is a single unnumbered prose sentence with no [1] marker; it is recorded as source bullet 1. There is no giver NPC and no hand-in -- the quest begins and ends on the Cermet Headstone, which is a targetable object and resolves as an npc key, so it carries the marker and start points at it too. The Flagellant's Rope is the header's Reward and therefore not evidence. The real gate is 'Zilart Mission 5 - Headstone Pilgrimage ACTIVATED (or already completed)': the header's Previous field is empty, and prev means completed, so putting the mission there would read as blocked for exactly the players who have it merely activated and are eligible. It is left out of prev and flagged instead. Fame 'Outlands' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.

steps.note: Zilart Mission 5 must be activated or already complete. The whole quest is this one trade -- there is nobody to report back to.

Both Belgidiveau and Novalmauge sit at (G-8) but in different zones -- Northern San d'Oria and Bostaunieux Oubliette -- which is a coincidence and not a grid conflict. notes: Same shape as Rivals, and handled the same way. Bullet 1 ('Obtain a Bone Chip from the Auction House or by farming Skeleton type mobs') is an acquisition instruction for the header's Item Reqs, not a rung; as its own first step with the chip as evidence it would blank the marker until the player happened to hold one, since neither the auction house nor 'Skeleton type mobs' is a targetable entity. It is merged into the trade step with both bullet numbers kept. No mob is recorded: 'Skeleton type mobs' is a FAMILY and not a name, and inventing 'Skeleton' would be exactly the guess this pass exists to avoid. The rewards -- the Dangruf Wadi map and 2000 experience -- prove the quest is over, not that a step is done, so evidence stays null throughout.
